title: VPC threat model and mTLS hardening notes
content:
Purpose:
This working note captures a compact threat model, concrete VPC patterns, firewall rules, mTLS rollout steps, RBAC v2 mapping for network controls, an audit log schema recommendation, and a practical evidence automation runbook for Private deployments. It is intended as a hands-on operational reference for engineers building customer-specific VPC/private deployments and SRE/security engineers owning evidence collection and SIEM exports.

Scope:
- Private deployment network layer only (VPCs, subnets, routing, firewalls, transit, load balancers)
- Mutual TLS between internal services and ingress edge
- Audit log schema for network-related events and RBAC changes
- SIEM export field mappings and retention pointers
- Evidence automation steps for customer audits (SOC2 / ISO style artifacts)

High-level threat model (top risks):
1) Unauthorized lateral movement after initial compromise of a host (insider or container breakout).
2) Misconfigured firewall/SG allowing broad access to control plane ports.
3) Compromised certificate/key leading to false mTLS identity.
4) Missing or sparse audit trails for network/routing changes.
5) Ineffective evidence packaging for customer audits (gaps in logs, missing signatures).

Design goals / mitigations summary:
- Zero-trust within VPC: least privilege SGs, deny-by-default NACLs where supported.
- mTLS enforced for all service-to-service traffic across trusted boundaries.
- RBAC v2 controls for who can modify network artifacts; changes require signed justification and ticket link.
- Audit-first: every network action emits structured audit events routed to SIEM and archived.
- Evidence automation: reproducible export with cryptographic signing and tamper-evident bundles.

VPC pattern recommendations:
- 3-tier VPC layout per deployment: control-plane subnet (private), serving subnet (private), management/egress subnet (private with NAT gateway).
- Dedicated customer VPCs for Private installs; when multi-tenant on-hosted private, use strict segmentation with transit gateways and isolation routes.
- Use AWS Transit Gateway / GCP VPC Peering with explicit route tables per service domain. Avoid transitive trust via flat route tables.

Example network diagram (ASCII):

  Internet --> Edge LB (public-subnet) --
                                   |
                               Firewall (WAF / AWS NACL / cloud FW)
                                   |
        +--------------------------+-------------------------+
        |                          |                         |
    Control Plane             Serving Pool             Management/Egress
  (private-subnet)        (private-subnet, autoscaled)   (private-subnet NAT)
        |                          |                         |
   KMS/HSM for certs       KV cache / LLM worker        Metrics / ELB egress

All inter-subnet traffic requires mTLS and limited SG rules (port ranges only).

Firewall / SG rule examples (AWS-style snippets):
- Load balancer -> edge-proxy: TCP 443, source 0.0.0.0/0 (receiver is LB, allow TLS only)
- edge-proxy -> service-proxy: TCP 8443, source = edge-proxy SG id (use SG refs, not IPs)
- service-proxy -> model-worker: TCP 5000-5100, source = service-proxy SG id
- control-plane -> kube-apiserver: TCP 6443, source = control-plane-bastion-cidr (narrow CIDR)
- management -> outbound to telemetry: TCP 9200 (ES), 6514 (syslog TLS), destination restricted to monitoring VPC

Notes: Prefer referencing security groups rather than wide CIDR ranges. For GCP use VPC Service Controls and firewall tags to emulate the same semantics.

mTLS rollout checklist (practical sequence):
1) Certificate policy: define short-lived certs (<=24h) for services, rotate roots quarterly. Store root and intermediates in KMS/HSM.
2) Implement cert issuance: small CA service (internal), with ACME-like automated issuance tied to service identity and RBAC checks.
3) Start with one service pair in canary mode: require mTLS but allow fallback and log failures (3 days).
4) Expand to service mesh sidecars (if using e.g., envoy/istio) configured in strict mTLS mode for internal traffic.
5) Enforce at external ingress: require client certs for control-plane endpoints or management APIs.
6) Hard fail enforcement: once telemetry shows <0.1% failures and runbooks validated, flip to deny fallback.

Sample certificate rotation command (kubectl/openssl example):
- Generate CSR locally: openssl req -new -nodes -out svc.csr -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout svc.key -subj "/CN=svc-name.cluster.local"
- Upload CSR to internal CA: curl -X POST -F "csr=@svc.csr" https://ca.internal/issue?role=service --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- CA returns cert PEM; store into KMS and mount into secret volume for the pod.

RBAC v2 mapping for network actions (recommendation):
- roles/network-admin: full CRUD on VPC, transit gateway, route tables (requires 2FA + approval).
- roles/network-operator: modify firewall rules curated by proposals, no VPC delete.
- roles/audit-reader: read-only access to all network audit logs and evidence bundles.
- roles/cert-manager: issue/renew certs but cannot modify route tables.
- Controls: require an attached ticket link and short justification for role elevation requests; elevation is time-bound.

Audit log schema (network & RBAC events) - recommended fields (structured JSON per event):
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- event_id: stable UUID
- event_type: e.g., "firewall.rule.add", "route.table.update", "cert.issued", "rbac.role.grant"
- actor: principal id (svc- or user-), identity provider id, auth method
- actor_ip: source IP where applicable
- target_resource: resource ARN/URL (e.g., vpc-1234, sg-5678)
- action: HTTP verb or action name (CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE/APPLY)
- change_summary: text description of delta (old/new) or patch
- justification_ticket: linked ticket id (JIRA/Confluence)
- correlation_id: request chain id to connect multi-hop actions
- success: boolean string ("true"/"false")
- evidence_blob: reference to signed artifact in evidence store (S3 path)
- signature: base64 signature field for tamper evidence

Note: In JSON logs, keep fields stable and avoid free-form text for key attributes so SIEM rules can reliably parse.

SIEM export and field mapping (example for Elasticsearch/Kibana index):
- index pattern: private-deployments-audit-*
- mapping: timestamp -> @timestamp (date), event_type -> keyword, actor -> keyword, target_resource -> keyword, success -> boolean, change_summary -> text, justification_ticket -> keyword, evidence_blob -> keyword, signature -> keyword
- recommended pipelines: ingest pipeline that verifies signature and flags tampering, geoip enrichment for actor_ip, and user mapping via idp lookup.

Evidence automation runbook (steps for a compliance snapshot):
1) Trigger: either scheduled weekly or via audit request.
2) Gather: pull audit index entries for timeframe, collect KMS key versions, export active SG/rule configs, route tables, and LB listener configs.
3) Package: place collected JSONs and config snapshots into a timestamped directory, sign manifest using deployment signing key (HSM), produce manifest.sig.
4) Verify: run checksum and signature verification, produce verification.log.
5) Publish: deliver to customer evidence bucket (S3/GCS) with restricted, time-limited link and retention metadata.
6) Record: create an immutable ticket entry with link to bundle, attach to audit log via evidence_blob references.

Automation script pseudocode (bash):
- set -e
- START=$(date -u -Iseconds -d "$1")
- END=$(date -u -Iseconds -d "$2")
- curl -s "$ELASTIC/_search?q=event_type:network* AND @timestamp:[${START} TO ${END}]&size=10000" > raw-audit.json
- terraform state pull --path aws_vpc > vpc-state.json || true
- aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters \"Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC_ID\" > sgs.json
- tar czf evidence-${START}_${END}.tgz raw-audit.json vpc-state.json sgs.json
- aws kms sign --key-id $SIGN_KEY --message fileb://evidence-${START}_${END}.tgz --output text --query Signature | base64 -d > evidence.sig
- aws s3 cp evidence-${START}_${END}.tgz s3://evidence-bucket/$DEPLOYMENT/ --acl private
- aws s3 cp evidence.sig s3://evidence-bucket/$DEPLOYMENT/ --acl private

Packaging and tamper-proofing:
- Use cloud provider KMS/HSM signing for manifests not just simple checksums.
- Keep signature verification code in a tiny reproducible repo that security owns.

Operational checks and SLOs for auditability:
- 99.9% of network change events must have a justification_ticket attached.
- Audit logs for network actions must be delivered to SIEM within 60s of event.
- Evidence bundles for scheduled snapshots must be produced within 30 minutes and signed.

Quick troubleshooting playbook (common failure modes):
- mTLS handshake failures: check cert chain expiry, mismatched CN/SAN, clock skew on node (NTP), missing intermediate certs.
- Missing audit log events: confirm logging agent is alive, ES ingest pipeline healthy, and forwarder to SIEM not backpressured.
- Evidence signature mismatch: ensure correct KMS key version, re-run signing step and compare key IDs.

Appendix: minimal checklists
A) Pre-deploy checklist (mandatory):
- Create RBAC roles for network-admin and network-operator and attach approval workflow.
- Ensure CA offline and online components defined; escrow root into HSM.
- Verify at least one canary service pair passes mTLS in strict mode.
- Confirm audit pipeline end-to-end (event -> SIEM index -> evidence bundle).

B) Hardening checklist (priority):
- [P0] Deny-by-default NACL and explicit allow SGs for all subnets.
- [P0] Enforce mTLS for all intra-VPC traffic across service boundaries.
- [P1] Rotate root/intermediate certs quarterly; record rotation event in audit log.
- [P1] SIEM pipeline verifies signature on audit logs and flags anomalies.
- [P2] Document and require ticket link on every network change; automate rejection of unauth'd changes.

C) Evidence delivery checklist (for customer audit):
- [ ] Signed manifest present and verification log included.
- [ ] Raw audit events for requested period included.
- [ ] Config snapshots for VPC, SGs, route tables, load balancer.
- [ ] KMS key versions and public key material included (private key never included).

References and next steps:
- Follow up: provide a small repo with the signing helper and a terraform data-export template.
- Proposed Jira epics: PD-2025 (evidence automation infra), PD-2026 (mTLS rollout automation), PD-2027 (RBAC v2 enforcement integration).

Open questions to resolve in next sync:
- How long should evidence bundles be retained for enterprise customers vs default (30/90/365 days)?
- Should we push for short-lived certs only, or allow a small set of long-lived service certs for legacy appliances?

Notes to self and action items:

- Priya to draft RBAC elevation workflow and sample UI text (due 2024-12-08).
- Asha to assemble small demo bundle for internal review and run a simulated audit (due 2024-12-18).
